item.title: 🟠 From One Account to Every Mailbox: Breaking Zimbra's Identity Boundaries (Part 1)
item.description:
Why this matters: Service impact is possible — verify vendor status before troubleshooting internally.

An enterprise mail server authenticates users, stores private communications, delivers recovery links, runs calendars, and sends mail that employees and other systems trust. Compromising it can therefore expose both email and the identities and workflows built around it.

During a broader assessment of Zimbra Collaboration Suite (ZCS), Rapid7 reported more than 80 vulnerabilities spanning authentication, mailbox authorization, calendar processing, web clients, document services, and the host operating system. The affected components are being fixed on different schedules, so we are publishing the analysis in stages. An accompanying GitHub repository containing full write-ups and PoCs serves as a live technical tracker, and will be updated as further findings and fixes become public.

item.description:

Overview

item.title: 🔴 Critical infrastructure orgs face heightened cyber risk from nation-state groups, AI threats
item.description:
Why this matters: Advanced threat activity — review privileged access, persistence detection, and lateral-movement controls.

Critical infrastructure faces mounting threats from nation-state groups and AI-driven attacks. In the latest installment of our Cybersecurity Awareness Month blog series, learn how leading cybersecurity agencies, such as CISA, are advising critical infrastructure organizations on ways to protect themselves and the essential services they provide.

Key takeaways

  1. Critical infrastructure organizations often struggle with asset visibility gaps that create hidden attack vectors. Many older OT systems are difficult to inventory, leaving them unmonitored and unpatched.
  2. Attackers are leveraging AI to map converged IT/OT networks at machine speed and exploit uninventoried legacy systems. Attackers are also using AI to attain the specialized know-how to breach complex industrial control systems.
  3. Iran-affiliated APT groups have attacked U.S. water, energy, and government facilities since the U.S. launched Operation Epic Fury in February, according to the U.S. government.
  4. As part of Cybersecurity Awareness Month, CISA is urging critical infrastructure operators to establish a solid cyber hygiene foundation, anchored on reducing vulnerabilities, replacing unsupported legacy devices, and preparing rapid recovery plans.

Source: Tenable Blog  |  Severity: Critical  |  Age: 1d

item.title: 🔴 Inside the Exchange Inspector: How Tenable uses OpenAI GPT cyber models to review open-source AI agents
item.description:
Why this matters: Supply-chain risk — review third-party access and affected vendor dependencies.

Community-built AI agents, skills, and MCP servers are landing in SOC workflows fast. Here’s what the Exchange Inspector tests before a listing earns its vetted tag on the CyberAgents Exchange.  Three tools have already passed.

Key takeaways

  1. Every Inspector-vetted listing clears three gates: an automated check, a frontier model assessment, and human verification. Tenable uses Tenable One AI Exposure to screen for prompt injection and exposed secrets, and OpenAI GPT Cyber models to assess the code and threat model. Tenable security researchers then verify runtime behavior in a clean environment. 
  2. The review tests 15 types of security issues across three layers of the stack. These issues range from conventional flaws like SSRF and path traversal vulnerabilities to agent-specific ones like excessive permissions and memory poisoning.
  3. Vetted tools are driving efficiencies: SOC Hunter has cut hunt times by 75% for Tenable’s security team. The CyberAgents Exchange currently has three Exchange Inspector-vetted listings: two built by Tenable and the other one by Splunk. These agents’ contributors report that they accelerate threat hunting, remediation triage, and cloud posture investigation.
